system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: We include all available information in the agent’s system prompt:
system_prompt_style.note: Paper-only. The system prompt includes the current code in view, the breakpoints, the last evaluation output and the last observation. These sections change between steps.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Repo directory tree: [Visible files in the repository, presented in the form of a directory tree. This is controlled by the .debugignore file.]
env_context_strategy.note: The directory tree is injected (depth 1 by default). The agent also navigates with the view/listdir tools.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: History of command and terminal outputs (the last 20 steps):
context_compaction.note: The user prompt carries a 20-step sliding window. This is paper-level agent behaviour only.

observation_format.evidence_quote: debug-gym represents observation information in structured text (e.g., JSON format)

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: The meta-syntax adopts the triple-backtick delimiter ``` from Markdown.
tool_call_format.note: The model emits a Markdown code block naming the tool (e.g. pdb c). None of the allowed values fits exactly. code_as_action is the closest because the action is a fenced block, but the block is tool syntax, not executable code. Flagged for Ambiguities.

tool_count.evidence_quote: We provide a preset of tools in the toolbox:
tool_count.note: Five tools are listed: eval, view, pdb, rewrite and listdir. The example agents use 3 or 4 of them. The count comes from the paper, not from a repository schema.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: When both line numbers are absent, it will perform in an identical manner as patchers that rewrite the entire file.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: An instructions attribute, which is a dictionary containing information about the tool that will be visible to the agent

protocol_standardization.note: Only the paper was available. No dependency list or source code to grep.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: At every step, an agent interacts with debug-gym via calling a tool from the set of available tools.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: our agents only involve minimal architectural de-sign and prompt optimization

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: We provide three example agents with debug-gym to showcase its API
multi_agent_topology.note: The paper names multi-agent reviewer systems only as future work.

delegation_mechanism.note: No agent registry or source code in the evidence.

human_in_loop.note: Paper-only. It says humans-in-the-loop agents are possible, but gives no gating mechanism.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: We keep a list of all breakpoints and restore them when there is a terminal session restarts.
short_term_state.note: Environment state holds the current working file, the breakpoints and the last eval output.

self_verification.evidence_quote: By default, this tool is automatically triggered after a rewrite action, but this can be modified by the user through configuration.

retry_policy.note: Paper-only. The paper runs each experiment 3 times for averaging, not as retries.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: An episode is terminated when either an agent has received a positive reward (success), or it has exhausted a pre-defined budget, in the form of the number of steps or the number of consumed tokens
termination_condition.note: The experiments also use a rewrite budget of 10.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: in the form of the number of steps or the number of consumed tokens (out of budget)

timeouts.evidence_quote: Despite having a timeout defined in debug-gym’s eval tool

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: debug-gym will copy the user-specified repository into a temporary working directory, which is by default mapped into a Docker container.
execution_isolation.note: A local terminal is available as an option.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: the specified files and directories are read only to an agent through debug-gym
filesystem_access.note: Relative to the container. Access is limited by .debugignore and .debugreadonly.

network_policy.note: No Docker config code in the evidence.

tracing.note: The paper mentions trajectories and logs, but not their format.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: we integrate three coding benchmarks into debug-gym

guardrails.evidence_quote: the read only setting can prevent agents from developing cheating strategies such as to pass the tests by editing or deleting them.

target_domain.evidence_quote: a textual environment, namely debug-gym, for developing LLM-based agents in an interactive coding setting

open_source.evidence_quote: We open source debug-gym at aka.ms/debug-gym.
open_source.note: No LICENSE file was available in the evidence.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: For closed-weights LLMs, we query them through online APIs, for open-weights ones, we host them using vLLM

primary_artifact.note: The repo exists, but only the report was in the evidence.

first_release_date.note: Fallback to the paper v1 date. No tag information was available.

pinned_version.note: No version or commit was given in the evidence.
